title: Engine Ignition: Component Locations
introduction:
I use this transparent engine drawing as an ignition map. Match its callouts to the Item and Description columns in the table. The blue coils form a row above the green spark-plug ends, showing how each coil sits at its plug. The transparent gray engine parts let you see that relationship; they do not show an access route with those parts removed.

The coil is an electrical transformer that produces the high voltage, and the plug provides the controlled gap where the spark starts combustion. Think of the coil as winding up the electrical punch and the plug as the place it lands. This reference identifies locations and relationships; plug specifications, cylinder numbering, testing and removal instructions belong to separate engine-specific information.

edits.why: Match the engine label before using the layout. Follow the blue coil bodies down toward the green plug ends, then use the unchanged table to identify each callout. A location drawing helps identify the parts; it cannot establish the cause of a misfire.
